prompt:
Backlog item: FIRST / BLOCKING: Starting a work session must put work on its own branch (and worktree) for isolation. work session == branch == own tree. This must hold for CliAgent, SubAgent, and no-agent flows ? not only CLI spawn. Today open/start of a work session can leave you on main/parent (e.g. C:\dev\abd-works-repo) so agents read/write the wrong tree. Fix at the work-session / start-ticket layer so every new work session binds to session/<name> with its own worktree before any job runs. After start-ticket, rebind workspace root to that worktree. Do this fix on the current branch first; later backlog items depend on it. (text).

Write failing tests before writing any fix. Read the ## Diagnosis in the ticket to determine which tests are required:

- PROMPT/AI CHANGE: write an agentic BDD test using /agent-bdd.development. This is the primary test type for prompt or instruction defects. A mechanical BDD test is rarely needed here — but not never; include one if the prompt change also has a verifiable mechanical side-effect.
- CODE CHANGE: write a mechanical (vanilla) BDD test using /bdd.development. Also write an agentic BDD test if the code defect was causing AI/agent misbehaviour.
- BOTH: write both. Mechanical BDD first.

The failing test is a hard requirement — write it first, run it, confirm it fails. You may alter existing tests or add new ones, but an explicit red test capturing the defect must exist before any fix is written.
judge_criteria: PASS only when: (1) at least one failing test exists that captures the defect; (2) for code changes: a mechanical BDD test is present; (3) for prompt/AI changes: an agentic BDD test is present; (4) mechanical BDD runs first when both are present; (5) tests were validated against the tools as normal.

Fix the defect using /clean_engineering.code in small iterations. Work one small piece at a time ? fix just enough to make one or a few tests pass, then move to the next piece. Repeat until all BDD and agentic BDD tests are green. Run vanilla BDD first when you have both.
Before writing any code: - Explore all impacted codebases and the code they depend on. - Read module-context.md for every module you touch. - Study the existing idioms, patterns, and usage in detail. Do not invent new patterns or paradigms ? follow what is already there. A defect fix should not require new patterns.
judge_criteria: PASS only when: (1) all BDD tests pass; (2) all agentic BDD tests pass; (3) the fix follows existing patterns, paradigms, and usage ? no new patterns invented without strong justification; (4) validated against the tools as normal.
